disease_label_per_paper: Legionnaires disease complicated by severe rhabdomyolysis, AKI requiring hemodialysis, and acute liver injury
presentation_summary: 32-year-old male with no prior medical history presented after 6 days of nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, reduced mobility, intermittent fever, shortness of breath, and minimal urine output.
Presentation vitals showed temperature 39.3 C, HR 108 bpm, BP 143/99 mmHg.
Chest X-ray showed right upper and middle lobe pneumonia; CT abdomen showed enterocolitis.
Initial labs: WBC 22.1 thou/mcL, sodium 128 mmol/L, creatinine 3.37 mg/dL, AST 1806 U/L, ALT 449 U/L, total bilirubin 3.6 mg/dL, lactate 3.2 mmol/L, CK >14000 U/L, later quantified at 201000 U/L.
Legionella urine antigen returned positive on hospital day 2; he required hemodialysis and escalation from azithromycin to levofloxacin.

quality_warnings: Legionella urine antigen is preserved as confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations. The ranking evidence emphasizes the clinical syndrome: pneumonia plus GI symptoms, hyponatremia, rhabdomyolysis, AKI, and transaminitis.
